transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-02-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 63 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Product), Samir (Harbor Head of ML), Ava (Harbor SRE), Diane (Harbor PM), Lewis (Harbor Security)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick intro — i'm lena, i'm the account lead. Marco will do the deep dive, priya will cover Optimize recs. Samir, do you want to kick off with a quick goal for today?

[00:18] Samir Patel: yeah thanks lena. goal is pretty pragmatic — we want to see how we can use redwood to run a structured output pipeline that calls our enrichment tools. primary constraints: sub-200ms p95 for small completions, data never leaves our vpc for PII paths, and we need reproducible outputs for audit.

[00:40] Marco Chen: great, that's exactly the kind of workflow JSON mode and sandbox tool calling were built for. i'll share my screen, i have a small live sandbox in the console — bear with me if the screen flickers.

[00:54] [screen share starts]

[01:02] Marco Chen: okay so first i want to show the API surface — here's a simple POST to /v1/completions with mode: "json" and a schema. the model returns typed objects, and if the model tries to deviate the runtime will apply the schema validator and attempt a structured fallback. so you get deterministic shapes.

[01:28] Ava Thompson: quick q — when you say "runtime will apply schema validator" is that server-side or client-side? we need to avoid any chance of PII being logged outside our control.

[01:40] Marco Chen: server-side in the customer's control plane for private deployments; for hosted we run validation before returning to the client but we can also perform validation in a private control plane with no telemetry. for dedicated customers you can enable "validate-only" within your VPC.

[01:58] Diane Park: and the sandbox for tool calling — does it actually execute customer tools or is it mocked?

[02:06] Marco Chen: good question. we have two modes: interactive sandbox and isolated execution. interactive sandbox can call pre-approved endpoints using a per-customer credential injection; isolated execution runs within a per-tenant sandbox that limits network egress and has a whitelist for allowed domains. both options produce audit logs.

[02:28] Lewis Grant: audit logs — is that the same as our SIEM ingest? can we forward to our Splunk? and what about key material, KMS?

[02:36] Priya Nair: yes, audit logs can be forwarded via syslog or direct S3 export to your account. KMS integrations are supported — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM-backed providers. for private deployments the key material never leaves the customer environment.

[02:54] [03:00] Marco Chen: switching to a short demo — i'll run a small pipeline: request enters -> JSON schema enforces fields: {"user_intent": string, "entities": [ {"type": string, "value": string} ], "actions": [ {"tool": string, "args": object} ] } — model produces structured actions, we validate, then the action runner calls the tool in the sandbox.

[03:32] Samir Patel: does the runner support retries and idempotence? our enrichment tools are eventually consistent and we can't have duplicate charges.

[03:40] Marco Chen: yes, action runner includes idempotency keys and you can configure at-least-once vs at-most-once semantics. we also tag the logs with action ids for tracing.

[03:54] [04:00] Ava Thompson: latency — when you call external tools from the sandbox does that add to p95 significantly?

[04:08] Marco Chen: it can, so we recommend two patterns: prefetch/cache enrichment results via a prefix/KV cache (that's what we call the KV cache) for hot keys, or run the action asynchronously and stream a partial response to the client while enrichment completes. Optimize can recommend which approach based on your traffic profile.

[04:30] Priya Nair: jumping in — i've prepared an Optimize run against a sample throughput. Optimize flags a few levers: increase batching for non-latency sensitive endpoints, enable per-route KV caching for repeated user ids, and a model quantization profile (4-bit for most tokens, fp16 for critical safety checks) to reduce cost by ~40% in our estimate.

[04:56] Diane Park: can you show the console flow for a canary rollout? we want to test a smaller model variant first and fall back if hallucination rates spike.

[05:04] Marco Chen: yep — in the Console you can define rollout policies: route 10% traffic to variant 'gptx-compact' and 90% to 'gptx-standard', set a guardrail on "structured validation failures" > 1% to automatically rollback. we'll surface token-level cost and validation failure rate on the route dashboard.

[05:26] Samir Patel: about hallucinations — can guardrails call a reranker or a validator service before committing an action?

[05:34] Marco Chen: absolutely. you can attach pre-commit hooks that call your internal validator. we suggest doing a lightweight syntactic validator in the runtime and an async semantic validator if it's heavier.

[05:46] [06:00] Lena Ortiz: this is all great. one more practical question — what's the onboarding time for a private VPC deployment? our compliance says we need dedicated private control plane.

[06:12] Marco Chen: typical private onboarding is 6–8 weeks: infrastructure provisioning, VPN/VPC peering, KMS integration, SOC2 paperwork, and performance tuning. we do a phased pilot — first dev sandbox, then staging with canary traffic, then production.

[06:30] Ava Thompson: can we run a smoke perf test on our logs with a 1-week benchmark? we want to see p95 behavior and cost per 1M tokens.

[06:38] Lena Ortiz: yes — next step we'll provision a short pilot. lena: action item — send pilot pricing and Dedicated options.

[06:46] [06:50] Marco Chen: i'm going to do a quick live trace — here i call the endpoint with schema and include a tool invocation: {"tool":"geocoding","args":{"addr":"50 Main St"}} — the runtime validates the JSON, then the sandbox calls the geocoding endpoint with restricted creds, returns a normalized {"lat":...,"lon":...}. note: in hosted we mask raw request payloads in logs by default; in private it's up to your retention policy.

[07:24] Samir Patel: wanted to surface a concern — our legal team insists on proof that no sensitive payloads are written to third-party logs. how proofy is your attestations?

[07:34] Priya Nair: we provide an audit package: architecture diagram, KMS key flows, and an attestations doc showing which components can see plaintext. for Dedicated/Private we can sign an addendum in the contract that specifies log retention and access controls.

[07:52] Lewis Grant: do you support SAML/SSO and per-route RBAC? we need least privilege for the action runner.

[07:58] Marco Chen: yes SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning for users, and fine-grained RBAC for routes/models/tools in the Console.

[08:12] [08:30] Marco Chen: ok now a brief detour — error scenarios. if the model returns malformed JSON we have auto-repair attempts: first we run a validator, if it fails we call the model in a restricted "repair" prompt (json-only) up to two times before we fallback to a safe default action or a human-in-the-loop. those retries are configurable.

[08:52] Samir Patel: what's the rate limit behavior when you have bursty traffic and Dedicated capacity has saturations? do you queue or spill to hosted variants?

[08:58] Marco Chen: policy-based routing — you can specify overflow to a cheaper hosted model with lower SLOs, or queue with a max-wait. we also support burst capacity via reserved spare slots. for compliance we can avoid routing PII paths outside the VPC.

[09:20] Ava Thompson: curious about cost math — how much does Optimize's recommendation actually save in practice?

[09:26] Priya Nair: in our reference workloads we see 30–50% savings by combining batching, prefix caching, and quantization. Optimize surfaces a prioritized list: expected saving, risk (quality delta), and recommended rollout plan.

[09:44] [10:00] Diane Park: any built-in testing harness for structured outputs? our QA wants to run a set of golden prompts and assert no regressions.

[10:08] Marco Chen: yes we expose an evals integration — you can upload prompt sets, expected schemas, and we run fuzz/regression tests across model variants. we'll send a link to the evals runbook.

[10:24] Samir Patel: how does function/tool calling differ from OpenAI's approach? are your tools typed and versioned?

[10:32] Marco Chen: our tools are first-class entities in the Console — each tool has a typed interface (schema), version history, and runtime constraints (timeout, retries, network egress). the runtime enforces types at call-time which reduces errors.

[10:50] [11:00] Lena Ortiz: ok let's pivot to the pricing ask — samir, do you have a budget window for this pilot?

[11:06] Samir Patel: yes we're looking at a 3-month pilot with a $25k–$50k expected spend, depending heavily on per-token price and whether Dedicated requires a commit.

[11:18] Lena Ortiz: fair. we'll include both a usage-based hosted option and a committed Dedicated option with a monthly minimum. i'll include the SLA and rollback commitments.

[11:28] [11:45] Marco Chen: closing the demo — i'll drop a couple of links in chat: sandbox guide, evals runbook, and a short KB on "schema enforcement and repair". also a small snippet showing the SDK call: POST /v1/actions {mode: "json", schema_id: "harbor_v1"}.

[11:58] Diane Park: will the pilot require a contract amendment for log retention terms?

[12:04] Lena Ortiz: likely yes for Dedicated/private; i'll have legal loop in. we'll do a short SOW for the pilot.

[12:12] [12:20] Samir Patel: thanks all, this was helpful. main concerns: latency at p95, guaranteed non-exfiltration of PII, and deterministic structured outputs. we'll review the materials and respond by end of week.

[12:34] Lena Ortiz: recap of next steps — (1) lena to send pilot pricing + sla doc, (2) marco to share quantization & config doc + small perf script, (3) ava to provide access to anonymized logs. we'll target a kickoff next tuesday if that works.

[12:52] [12:58] Marco Chen: thanks everyone. i'll follow up in email with the links and a proposed benchmark script.

[13:04] Meeting end

Notes: minor ASR errors present — some product names transcribed as "gptx" or "geo coding". Shared links: sandbox guide: https://tinyurl.com/redwood-sandbox-guide | evals runbook: https://tinyurl.com/redwood-evals | pilot pricing doc (draft): https://tinyurl.com/redwood-pilot-draft
